meaning: Short and detached: about 50 percent of the grid step (0.125 beat on sixteenths). Staccatissimo goes down to 33 or 25 percent. In the note list the share is the gate.
Held for the whole grid step, 100 percent of the step.
Between staccato and tenuto: 67 or 75 percent of the step. Sources disagree on the figure.
A pushed, accented note at about 67 percent of the step.
Smooth and joined: each note starts before the one before it ends. A mono synth needs this overlap to glide or hold its envelopes.

controls.label: Legato
controls.step: turn on so the held note keeps its envelopes

meaning: Two notes of the same pitch merged into one longer note. No single note rule carries this.
Notes held long: pads hold the chord span, and a sustained bass changes every 4 or 8 beats.
Short notes of 0.25 to 0.5 beat.
A note of at most 0.5 beat.
A note of at least 2 beats.
Notes of at most half a step, separated by uneven rests.
Slide from one pitch to the next by overlapping the two notes. The preset needs mono mode, legato on and a portamento time above zero.

controls.label: Portamento Time
controls.step: about 80 to 150 ms, longer for a swoop

meaning: A flagged acid step glides into the next, and the slide gate starts one step later. Slide only 15 to 35 percent of the notes. Glide time is 60 to 120 ms.
An accented acid step: velocity 100 to 127 against 70 to 90 for the rest. The preset must send velocity to level and cutoff, or the accent is silent.

controls.label: Velocity Track
controls.step: set above 0 percent so velocity opens level and tone

meaning: A mono 808 glide: the end of one note overlaps the next and the notes run long. Glide time is 80 to 150 ms, fast 30 to 50 ms, slow 200 ms and more.

controls.label: Portamento Time
controls.step: 80 to 150 ms; fast 30 to 50 ms; slow 200 ms and more

meaning: The dynamic mark pp (very quiet) as velocity 32 to 39.
The dynamic mark p (quiet) as velocity 48 to 61.
The dynamic mark mp (medium quiet) as velocity 64 to 71.
The dynamic mark mf (medium loud) as velocity 80 to 84.
The dynamic mark f (loud) as velocity 96 to 98.
The dynamic mark ff (very loud) as velocity 112 to 113.
The dynamic mark fff (fortississimo, the loudest) as velocity 126 to 127.
The number of notes that can sound at once. In Serum 2 the POLY limit may count unison voices as voices. It is a preset matter.

controls.label: Polyphony
controls.step: voice count; allow for unison voices

meaning: The bass plays the chord root. Psytrance sits at pitches 29 to 33 and rolling techno at 43.
Bass on the eighth offbeats, slots 2, 6, 10 and 14, with notes of 0.25 to 0.5 beat. Melodic techno alternates velocity 100 and 85, with a ghost at slot 15 at 60 to 70.

The psytrance and techno bass grid: kick on every beat and a bass note on each other sixteenth, 12 per bar on one pitch. Notes are equal in velocity, 0.125 to 0.19 beat long (gate 60) and never legato.

ask.question: Is the rolling line a bass grid, a drum and bass bass line, or a hat roll?
ask.when: The request asks for a drum and bass bass line. Every other request takes the bass grid.

meaning: In drum and bass, either a busy top loop under simple drums or a busy mid bass over a steady sub. It has no note grid.
A trap hat roll: repeated hi-hat hits that rise in velocity into the snare. See the named rhythm hat roll.
The bass plays the root, then the note seven semitones above it.

One note per beat, slots 0, 4, 8 and 12, each 0.9 to 1.0 beat. Beat 1 is the root, beat 3 a chord tone, and beat 4 an approach note a semitone from the next root. A pitch is not repeated twice in a row.
One bass pitch held or repeated for 4 or more bars while the chords above change.
The bass onsets equal the kick onsets, as in 808, trap and dubstep. House and techno do the opposite and play in the gaps. No single note rule relates two parts.
A detuned, growling bass whose notes last 1 beat or more.
A bass whose filter is moved by a fast LFO. The rate is a preset matter. In MIDI it is one sustained note per phrase, 1 to 4 beats long.
The catchy short melody, a lead of 2 to 6 distinct pitches over 1 to 2 bars, repeated. An uplifting trance motif has 4 to 6 notes over 8 bars.
A short repeating figure of 1 to 2 bars.
The same pitches and rhythm repeated for 4 or more bars.
Two phrases of equal length. The first ends off the tonic, on the 2nd, 5th or flat 7th, and the second ends on the root.
The last beat or bar of a 4 or 8 bar phrase gets denser, such as a snare roll that speeds up and rises in velocity.
A long, slow glide into a lead note, 150 to 300 ms, by overlapping the notes.
The notes of a chord played one at a time, sorted by pitch, one per step. A step of 1/8 is 0.5 beat, 1/16 is 0.25 and 1/16T is 0.1667. Gate is a share of the step.
The chord notes climb from low to high, then start again.
The chord notes fall from high to low, then start again.
Up, then down. The period is 2N-2 steps for N chord notes without repeated end notes, and 2N with them. Manuals differ.
The trance pattern: root, 3rd, 5th, octave, 5th, 3rd. Six notes realign with the bar every 3 bars. Gate is 60 to 70 percent of the step.
The chord starts on slot 0 of its first bar and lasts the whole chord span.
A short chord hit of 0.25 to 0.5 beat. Offbeat house places it on slots 2, 6, 10 and 14. The role entry decides the sound.
Chords 0.75 beat apart: slots 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12.

The chords breathe with the kick, which compression makes. In MIDI, sustain full-bar chords and leave slot mod 4 of 0 empty in the bass. The first bass note after the kick may be 30 percent quieter or 5 to 15 ms later.
A chopped pad. In MIDI it is one held chord. An LFO or step pattern on volume makes the chop, 16 steps per bar at 136 to 140 BPM.
